system.description:
Origins

The Tau are an enigmatic people with little talent for magic and an even smaller role than humans in the politics of the Astral Sea. They have never left their native crystal sphere and almost never receive visitors: their Portal Relay has not been activated, and their sphere is surrounded by a barrier known as the Wall of Fire, which makes any approach close to suicide.

Physically they are humanoid and walk on cloven hooves. Their grey-blue skin is tough and leathery and does not sweat, a legacy of their arid homeworld. Their faces are flat and broad at the eyes; the organs of smell sits inside the mouth. Their eyes perceive infrared and ultraviolet, though they need longer than humans to bring faraway things into focus.

Appearance

Tau look quite unlike most races of the Wheel. On average they are somewhat frailer than humans, though this owes as much to their society as to biology: those who take up manual work or close combat become just as powerful as humans or Squats, if with a little more effort. Descended from plains-dwelling creatures, they sprint well and walk long distances with ease. Their widely spaced eyes are slow to focus at range, which their excellent sense of smell partly makes up for — something they regret around Orks or halflings. On their own they only ever developed healing and protective sorcery.

In Play

Unlike the other peoples of the Wheel, the Tau live under a single government devoted to the collective Greater Good rather than greed or personal ambition, and they teach that the welfare of the whole matters more than that of any individual. Early in life, genetic and standardised tests assign each Tau the role they are best suited for and will most enjoy; they admit it disappoints the occasional Tau who longs for a role they are unsuited to, but consider it best for everyone.

Their castes resemble the Squats' but are more absolute and even genetically distinct; mates from outside one's caste are so rare that the castes may one day become separate species. Tau rarely think of themselves first, although those placed in command reason independently very well. They will listen to anyone's suggestions, but an unqualified opinion carries little weight — if that person were truly fit to advise, why are they not in that post already?

Tau technology looks clean and elegant but is actually somewhat behind the average. Unable to open Portal Relays, they have expanded slowly, and their scant knowledge of sorcery leaves them vulnerable to nearly any magical threat.

Example heroes (p. 58): Shas'la Kais, O'Shaserra, O'Shovah.

power.name: Fall Back
power.description: When a Dodge against any attack succeeds, you can take a free Withdraw action at half the normal distance.
